usage_by_team.primary_pattern: Isolated worktree parallelism with file-based consolidation. No inter-agent communication during execution. Coordinator merged results post-hoc from worktree outputs.
Phase-gated sequential handoff. Research teams wrote files consumed by software team in next phase. Coordinator routed findings manually between teams.
Solo agent with no communication needs. Single software engineer iterating on code.
Coordinator-mediated file exchange. 12 agents + 8 subagents across 8 teams. Coordinator had read-only access to all outputs and produced a cross-team synergy report. No live messaging.
Solo research agent. No inter-agent communication needed.
Solo research agent cataloging APIs. No communication.
Two-phase parallel with file handoff. 9 agents across research and software teams. No live communication -- phase boundary was the synchronization point.
Solo research agent designing JSONL bus. Produced KB-0015 as the bus specification. No communication used or needed.
Solo research agent designing SQLite WAL state. Produced KB-0016. No communication.
Solo failure mode analyst. Produced KB-0017. No communication.
Build-test-fix loop across 7 subagents. Communication was sequential handoff: build team writes code, test team runs tests, fix team patches bugs. 4 iterations. File-based coordination.
Solo architecture analyst. No communication needed.
Hub-coordinated parallel teams. 8+ teams (3 programming, 3 research, 2 think tanks). Coordinator mediated via file outputs. Built SDK launcher system but did not use Proto A for own coordination.
First Proto A dogfooding. 3 think tanks communicated via JSONL bus: 31 messages across 3 channels (global, topic-think-tank, topic-insights). Active cross-referencing of findings in real-time.

First production Proto A deployment. 18 agents, 6 teams. 47 messages across 3 channels. bus_cli.py as primary interface. File-based outputs for persistence (157KB). No help_protocol, direct_channels, or work_stealing (not yet built).

Design-to-implementation pipeline. 7 teams (~20 agents). Think tanks designed features, coding teams implemented them. Bus used for coordination. Created help_protocol, direct_channels, and work_stealing modules.

Simultaneous stress testing. 7 teams all parallel. Think tanks analyzed code, coding teams wrote stress tests, research team studied best practices. Bus for coordination, file outputs for results. 96 stress tests produced.

Most comprehensive Proto A usage. 15 teams in 3 batches. Used help_protocol for idle team reassignment (user directive), coordinator_hub for monitoring. Bug fixes applied to all 3 coordination modules. Anti-sequential enforcement.
Solo coding team doing data quality fixes. No communication needed.
4 parallel audit teams with coordinator. Completed in ~90 seconds. No Proto A used -- pure file-based parallel execution. Demonstrates that simple parallel tasks do not need the coordination stack.

7 teams with Proto A bus: 12 dedicated channels (3 per TT-RT pair plus global/bug). Researchers published to bus channels, think tanks consumed paired channels. Bug monitor checked bus integrity. Most structured channel usage observed.

Full pipeline execution using all Proto A primitives. 8 teams through 5-stage pipeline with PipelineManager. WorkStealing for task distribution. Scratchpad for cross-stage data. DirectChannels for progress. 2 complete iterations. Most complete Proto A integration.
4-phase analysis pipeline. 8 teams across phases. File-based outputs between phases. No Proto A coordination despite being a late session. Phase boundaries used as sync points.

communication_audit.most_used: bus (JSONL message bus) - Used by 7 of 28 sessions. The bus was the first Proto A feature available and the primary coordination mechanism. bus_cli.py became the standard interface after TEAM-0022. Total tracked messages: 47 (T-0022) + 31 (T-0021) + 12+ channels (T-0028) + messages across T-0023/0024/0025.
communication_audit.least_used: help_protocol - Only 2 sessions actively used help_protocol (TEAM-0025 with user-directed reassignment, TEAM-0022_pipeline). Despite being designed to solve the idle-team problem identified in the original TEAM-0022, auto_assign_idle_teams() was never integrated into multi_team_runner.py's monitoring loop. work_stealing was similarly underutilized in practice -- only TEAM-0022_pipeline used it for actual work distribution.

phase_1_pre_proto_a.pattern: File-based coordination. Git worktrees for isolation. Coordinator as manual router. Phase-gated sequential handoffs.
phase_1_pre_proto_a.communication: Zero live inter-agent messaging. All coordination through file outputs and sequential phase boundaries.

phase_2_bus_only.pattern: JSONL bus for messages, file outputs for persistence. bus_cli.py as CLI wrapper.
phase_2_bus_only.communication: Live messaging via bus channels. 31-47 messages per session. Topic-based channel organization.

phase_3_full_stack.pattern: Bus + help_protocol + direct_channels + work_stealing + scratchpad + coordinator_hub.
phase_3_full_stack.communication: Full coordination stack available. Named channels, progress broadcasting, work queue, pipeline DAGs.

phase_4_regression.pattern: Reverted to file-based coordination despite full stack being available.
phase_4_regression.communication: No Proto A used. Simpler tasks did not justify coordination overhead, or teams were unaware of available tools.

efficiency_patterns.pattern: Cross-team finding cross-referencing via bus channels
efficiency_patterns.evidence: TEAM-0021: 31 bus messages enabled Think Tank Gamma to integrate Alpha's overhead analysis and Beta's throughput data in real-time. TEAM-0022_original: Alpha-1 and Alpha-2 cross-referenced to discover the benchmark vs live test contradiction -- Alpha-1 alone would have concluded Proto A is broken, but Alpha-2's context revealed the benchmark config bug.
efficiency_patterns.impact: HIGH - Catches contradictions and produces insights no single team could achieve. The benchmark bug discovery (rate limiter denying 64.6% of requests) is the strongest evidence of multi-team communication value across the entire repository history.

efficiency_patterns.pattern: bus_cli.py as universal CLI interface (CLI-first pattern)
efficiency_patterns.evidence: TEAM-0022_original validated bus_cli.py as the primary communication pattern for 18 agents across 6 teams. Decoupled agents from Python import paths. Any agent that can execute bash can participate. Extended in TEAM-0023 with 7 new commands. Documented in efficiency_guide.json as EFF-006.
efficiency_patterns.impact: HIGH - Eliminated import path issues. Made coordination accessible to all agent types regardless of Python environment. Became the standard interface for all subsequent Proto A usage.

efficiency_patterns.evidence: TEAM-0025: User corrected coordinator's initial sequential plan, enforcing all teams within each batch to run simultaneously. TEAM-0027: Full repo audit completed in 90 seconds with 4 parallel teams (impossible sequentially). SOP-011 formalized 10 Anti-Sequential Rules (ASR-001 through ASR-010).
efficiency_patterns.impact: HIGH - TEAM-0027's 90-second audit is the clearest efficiency demonstration. Hard Dependency Test from SOP-011: 'Does Task B require a specific computed artifact that only Task A can produce?' If no, run in parallel.

efficiency_patterns.evidence: TEAM-0028: Created 12 dedicated channels (3 per think-tank/researcher pair plus global/bug channels). Researchers published structured findings to paired channels. Think tanks consumed only their paired channel, reducing noise. Most structured channel usage observed.
efficiency_patterns.impact: MEDIUM - Reduced global bus noise. Each think tank received only relevant findings from its paired researcher. Better signal-to-noise than broadcasting everything to global channel.

efficiency_patterns.evidence: TEAM-0022_pipeline: 8 teams through 5-stage pipeline (research_and_plan -> programming -> testing -> bug_fixing -> convergence_and_archive). PipelineManager enforced stage ordering, preventing premature advancement. 2 complete iterations with proper dependency enforcement.
efficiency_patterns.impact: MEDIUM - Replaced ad-hoc phase gating with formal DAG-based dependency tracking. Auto-trigger of downstream stages eliminated manual coordination. Required explicit get_ready_stages() call to promote stages (a gotcha that was documented for future teams).

efficiency_patterns.pattern: Scratchpad for cross-stage data (not bus messages)
efficiency_patterns.evidence: TEAM-0022_pipeline: Used scratchpad for sharing implementations from Stage 2 (programming) to Stage 3 (testing) without bus message size limits. Documented in efficiency_guide.json as EFF-004. Bus messages capped at 4096 bytes; scratchpad has no practical limit (1MB values tested in stress tests).
efficiency_patterns.impact: MEDIUM - Eliminated message splitting for large payloads. Reliable key-based lookup instead of ad-hoc file discovery. JSON-serializable with configurable TTL.

efficiency_patterns.evidence: TEAM-0022_original produced 157KB of structured JSON output across 5 team files. Think tank convergence (think_tank.py) could aggregate at any time. Documented in efficiency_guide.json as EFF-008. Contrast with pre-Proto-A teams where findings were only written at session end.
efficiency_patterns.impact: MEDIUM - Zero data loss from team crashes. Enables mid-session convergence analysis. Other teams see findings in real-time.

efficiency_patterns.pattern: Solo agents for focused research tasks
efficiency_patterns.evidence: TEAM-0015 (bus design), TEAM-0016 (SQLite WAL design), TEAM-0017 (failure analysis), TEAM-0019 (architecture analysis) all completed high-quality KB entries as solo agents. KB-0030 confirmed solo agents are most efficient at 4.0 artifacts/agent vs 0.44 for 27-agent teams.
efficiency_patterns.impact: HIGH - 89% per-agent efficiency drop in large teams. Solo agents produce the highest quality-per-resource for independent research tasks that have no data dependencies.

inefficiency_patterns.pattern: Idle team waste -- teams finishing early with no reassignment mechanism
inefficiency_patterns.evidence: TEAM-0022_original: 5 teams sat idle while Beta-1 was still processing all KB entries and session logs. Beta-1 became the bottleneck for the entire session. This directly motivated TEAM-0023's creation of help_protocol.py. Even after help_protocol existed, auto_assign_idle_teams() was never integrated into multi_team_runner.py.
inefficiency_patterns.cost: HIGH - Wasted capacity proportional to the gap between fastest and slowest team. In an 18-agent deployment, potentially 14+ agents sat idle waiting for 4 agents on Beta-1. Estimated 40-60% of total agent-time wasted.

inefficiency_patterns.pattern: Coordination tools built but never fully deployed (build-not-use gap)
inefficiency_patterns.evidence: help_protocol.py (698 lines), direct_channels.py (589 lines), work_stealing.py (677 lines), coordinator_hub.py (612 lines), sdk_launcher.py (~500 lines), sdk_config.py (~400 lines), sdk_cli.py (~600 lines), sdk_dashboard.py (~500 lines) -- totaling 4,500+ lines of coordination code. Yet TEAM-0026, TEAM-0027, and TEAM-0029 reverted to file-based coordination. bus_cli.py only covers help_protocol commands; direct_channels and work_stealing still lack CLI commands as of TEAM-0024 handoff.
inefficiency_patterns.cost: HIGH - 7 consecutive inward-facing teams (T22-T28) spent the majority of their time building coordination infrastructure that was rarely used in production. KB-0030 flagged this as a critical recursion risk. Zero market research picks logged despite SOP-018 existing.

inefficiency_patterns.evidence: TEAM-0025: User had to correct the coordinator's initial wave-based sequential plan. SOP-011 documented 6 root causes of sequential defaulting: risk aversion without visibility (SEQ-001), causal dependency assumption (SEQ-002), simpler mental model (SEQ-003), past merge conflicts (SEQ-004), completion dependency illusion (SEQ-005), no partial result consumption (SEQ-006).
inefficiency_patterns.cost: MEDIUM - Sequential execution of independent tasks wastes time linearly with the number of teams. The Hard Dependency Test is rarely applied -- coordinators default to sequences unless explicitly corrected.

inefficiency_patterns.pattern: API documentation mismatch causing integration friction
inefficiency_patterns.evidence: TEAM-0022_pipeline found 5 API mismatches: Scratchpad(key, value, namespace, ttl) vs documented (namespace, key, value, ttl_seconds), DirectChannels.set_presence vs documented update_presence, DirectChannels.update_progress vs documented broadcast_progress, PipelineManager requires team+agent_id not documented, get_ready_stages() required before start_stage() not documented.
inefficiency_patterns.cost: MEDIUM - Each mismatch costs debugging time. With 5 mismatches across 3 modules, teams waste significant effort discovering actual API signatures. KB entries and SOPs become unreliable references.

inefficiency_patterns.pattern: Bus integrity issues from non-BusWriter usage
inefficiency_patterns.evidence: TEAM-0028 bug monitor found 95 issues: 30 schema violations (agents bypassing BusWriter), 58 invalid message types (non-Proto A code writing to bus files), 7 source code bugs. Messages written by non-BusWriter code are invisible to BusReader, causing silent data loss.
inefficiency_patterns.cost: MEDIUM - 30 messages effectively lost. Bus reliability degrades when agents write directly to JSONL files instead of using BusWriter.publish(). No enforcement mechanism prevents direct writes.

inefficiency_patterns.pattern: No SharedState DB initialization in deployments
inefficiency_patterns.evidence: TEAM-0028 bug monitor: 'No SharedState DB initialized -- heartbeats, rate limiting, phase signals non-functional.' 53 expired messages uncleaned (no EpochRotator running). Deployments used the bus but skipped initializing the full state layer.
inefficiency_patterns.cost: MEDIUM - Heartbeat monitoring, rate limiting, and phase signals were all non-functional. The coordination system was partially deployed, missing its state management layer. Dead agent detection could not function.

inefficiency_patterns.evidence: TEAM-0022_original: Beta-1 was assigned to 'index all 20 KB entries + 17 team session logs' as a single monolithic task. Other idle teams could not help because the work was not decomposed. Documented as anti-pattern AP-002 in efficiency_guide.json.
inefficiency_patterns.cost: MEDIUM - Single team becomes critical path. No opportunity for work redistribution. Direct cause of the idle-team waste in IP-001.

inefficiency_patterns.pattern: Knowledge loss from missing session logs and handoff artifacts
inefficiency_patterns.evidence: 4 team session logs missing (TEAM-0011, -0015 root copies in wrong location, -0016, -0017). KB-0011 lost content (replaced with placeholder). KB-0012 content duplicates KB-0013. TEAM-0015/0016/0017 session logs existed only in teams/ root, not in teams/sessions/ as expected. Documented as anti-pattern AP-010.
inefficiency_patterns.cost: MEDIUM - Future teams cannot build on lost knowledge. The prime directive ('every AI team builds on the knowledge of the last team') is violated. 4 sessions worth of context permanently unavailable.

inefficiency_patterns.pattern: Overproduction of SOPs and coordination infrastructure (recursion trap)
inefficiency_patterns.evidence: KB-0030: 7 consecutive inward-facing teams (T22-T28). 13 SOPs approaching saturation. SOP-018 (Market Research) never executed. SOP-023 anti-recursion rule proposed 60/30/10 domain/infra/overhead ratio. Zero market research picks logged despite elaborate picks system and 47 AI-quant techniques documented.
inefficiency_patterns.cost: HIGH - The coordination system became its own purpose rather than serving domain work. Teams spent more time improving coordination than doing domain work. The infrastructure is feature-complete but under-exercised in real operations.

recommendations.recommendation: Integrate auto_assign_idle_teams() into multi_team_runner.py monitoring loop immediately
recommendations.rationale: The single highest-cost inefficiency (IP-001) was idle teams, which motivated creating help_protocol.py. But the integration into the actual runner was never done. The function exists, is tested (80/80 + 96 stress tests pass), but is not called during real operations. This is a 1-line integration that could recover 40-60% of wasted agent-time.

recommendations.recommendation: Add bus_cli.py commands for direct_channels and work_stealing modules
recommendations.rationale: bus_cli.py is the validated CLI-first interface (EP-002). But it only covers help_protocol. Direct_channels and work_stealing lack CLI commands, forcing Python imports. This was flagged in TEAM-0023 handoff, TEAM-0024 handoff, and TEAM-0025 handoff -- 3 consecutive teams noted this gap without fixing it. Until CLI commands exist, these modules will remain underutilized.

7 consecutive inward-facing teams is the most concerning pattern in the repository. The coordination system is feature-complete. No new SOPs or coordination modules should be created until at least 3 consecutive domain-work sessions are completed (market research, data gathering, or other external-facing work).

recommendations.recommendation: Mandate SharedState DB initialization in all Proto A deployments
recommendations.rationale: TEAM-0028 found heartbeats, rate limiting, and phase signals were non-functional because SharedState DB was never initialized. Add a pre-flight check to multi_team_runner.py that verifies DB initialization before launching any teams. Without this, the coordination system is running at partial capability.

recommendations.recommendation: Adopt paired channel architecture as default for research-analysis workflows
recommendations.rationale: TEAM-0028's 12-channel paired architecture (researcher -> think tank) produced the most structured and lowest-noise communication pattern observed. Should be the default template for any workflow with data-gathering and analysis teams. Document as SOP addendum to SOP-013.

recommendations.recommendation: Fix all 5 documented API mismatches between KB entries and actual module signatures
recommendations.rationale: TEAM-0022_pipeline discovered 5 API documentation mismatches that cause integration friction. KB entries and SOPs that reference incorrect signatures mislead new teams. Update KB-0023, KB-0024, and tool_sops.json with correct signatures.

recommendations.recommendation: Apply Hard Dependency Test (SOP-011) before any multi-team operation planning
recommendations.rationale: Sequential defaulting (IP-003) was observed even in TEAM-0025 despite extensive anti-sequential documentation. The Hard Dependency Test should be a mandatory pre-planning step: 'Does Task B require a specific computed artifact that only Task A can produce, AND that artifact does not exist yet?' If no, run in parallel.

recommendations.recommendation: Use solo agents for independent research tasks, teams of 5-8 for integrated operations
recommendations.rationale: Three independent analyses (KB-0030, TEAM-0028 TT-1, TEAM-0028 TT-3) all converged on 5-10 agent optimal team size. Solo agents produce 4.0 artifacts/agent. Teams of 20+ lose 89% per-agent efficiency. SOP-022 provides the detailed team sizing rules.

recommendations.recommendation: Enforce BusWriter.publish() as the only way to write to bus channels
recommendations.rationale: 30 schema-violating messages found by TEAM-0028 bug monitor from agents bypassing BusWriter. These messages are invisible to BusReader, causing silent data loss. Consider making bus files read-only at the filesystem level and providing BusWriter as the sole write path.

recommendations.recommendation: Decompose large tasks into WorkStealing queue items before assigning to teams
recommendations.rationale: The monolithic task assignment pattern (IP-007) directly causes idle-team waste. When Beta-1 was assigned all 20 KB entries as one task, no redistribution was possible. If each KB entry had been a separate WorkStealing item, idle teams could have helped process them in parallel.

metrics_framework.why: The #1 inefficiency observed was idle teams (IP-001). In TEAM-0022_original, estimated utilization was ~40% due to 14+ agents waiting for Beta-1. This metric directly measures the cost of the idle-team problem.

Measures communication efficiency. TEAM-0021 had 31 messages for ~10 findings (3.1 msg/finding). TEAM-0022_original had 47 messages for 30 findings (1.6 msg/finding). Lower is better -- indicates teams are producing findings rather than generating coordination noise.

Measures how quickly the communication system enables cross-pollination. TEAM-0021's think tanks began cross-referencing within the first few minutes. The benchmark bug discovery in TEAM-0022 was the highest-value cross-team finding.

TEAM-0021 measured I/O overhead at 0.047% of runtime. But TEAM-0028 TT-1 measured broader coordination overhead at 15-30% (orphan files, unresolved items). The gap between I/O cost and total coordination cost is the real overhead to track.

7 consecutive inward-facing teams (T22-T28) is the clearest sign of recursion trap. This metric enforces the 60/30/10 ratio. Zero market research picks despite 47 documented techniques shows the imbalance.

Measures whether the help protocol actually resolves idle-team waste. Currently unmeasurable because help_protocol is almost never used in production (IP-002). Once integrated, this tracks whether idle teams are successfully reassigned.

Measures whether decomposed work actually gets completed. TEAM-0024 stress tests found zombie work items (claimed but never completed) as a failure mode. This metric catches work items falling through the cracks.

TEAM-0028 found 30 schema violations from agents bypassing BusWriter. Non-compliant messages are invisible to BusReader, causing silent data loss. This metric tracks whether all agents are using the standard write path.
4 missing session logs out of 28 (86% completion). Knowledge loss from missing logs violates the prime directive. This metric ensures future teams leave proper documentation.
Tracks whether adding more agents actually produces more output. KB-0030 showed solo agents at 4.0 artifacts/agent vs 0.44 for 27-agent teams. If this metric drops below 1.0, the team is too large.

summary.key_finding: The coordination system is technically sound (80/80 unit tests + 96 stress tests pass, <1% I/O overhead) but operationally underdeployed. Only 25% of sessions used Proto A. Of the 4,500+ lines of coordination code built, only the JSONL bus is regularly used. help_protocol, work_stealing, and scratchpad are almost never used in production despite being the solutions to the most observed inefficiency (idle team waste). The biggest risk is not a technical failure but an organizational one: 7 consecutive teams spent time building coordination infrastructure instead of using it for domain work.
